A limb or appendage that an animal uses for support or locomotion on land.

examples.text: Insects have six legs.

glosses: In humans, the lower limb extending from the groin to the ankle.

examples.text: Dan won't be able to come to the party, since he broke his leg last week and is now on crutches.

glosses: The portion of the lower limb of a human that extends from the knee to the ankle.
A part of garment, such as a pair of trousers/pants, that covers a leg.

examples.text: The left leg of these jeans has a tear.

glosses: A rod-like protrusion from an inanimate object, such as a piece of furniture, supporting it from underneath.

examples.text: the legs of a chair or table

glosses: Something that supports.

examples.text: This observation is an important leg of my argument.

glosses: A stage of a journey, race etc.

examples.text: After six days, we're finally in the last leg of our cross-country trip.

glosses: A distance that a sailing vessel does without changing the sails from one side to the other.
One side of a multiple-sided (often triangular) course in a sailing race.
A single game or match played in a tournament or other sporting contest.

examples.text: A stunning performance from the Republic of Ireland all but sealed progress to Euro 2012 as they crushed nine-man Estonia 4-0 in the first leg of the qualifying play-off tie in A Le Coq Arena in Tallinn.

glosses: One of the two sides of a right triangle that is not the hypotenuse.
One of the two equal sides of an isosceles triangle.
One of the branches of a hyperbola or other curve which extend outward indefinitely.
The ability of something to persist or succeed over a long period of time.

examples.text: This proposal has no legs. Almost everyone opposes it.
I’m trying to go with my head and focus on the first guy, because this could be a relationship with legs.

glosses: A disreputable sporting character; a blackleg.

An extension of a steam boiler downward, in the form of a narrow space between vertical plates, sometimes nearly surrounding the furnace and ash pit, and serving to support the boiler; called also water leg.
In a grain elevator, the case containing the lower part of the belt which carries the buckets.
Denotes the half of the field on the same side as the batsman's legs; the left side for a right-handed batsman.

examples.text: Ponsonby-Smythe hit a thumping drive through the leg fielders.

glosses: A branch or lateral circuit connecting an instrument with the main line.
A branch circuit; one phase of a polyphase system.
An underlying instrument of a derivatives strategy.
An army soldier assigned to a paratrooper unit who has not yet been qualified as a paratrooper.

examples.text: Which was lower than whale shit in the eyes of any paratrooper; it would have been a disgrace to be a leg.

glosses: A gesture of submission; a bow or curtsey. Chiefly in phrase make a leg.

examples.text: Hickman came in, making his legs, and stroking his cravat and ruffles.

glosses: A column, as a unit of length of text as laid out.

examples.text: A leg is one column of a story. It has two legs if it is set in two columns and three legs if it is set in three columns. Avoid legs longer than 10 inches and shorter than 1 inch.

glosses: Synonym of leg up (“forming a step for a person's feet with one's hands”).

examples.text: The street was deserted. We acted quickly. Josiah gave me a leg. I threw my jacket over the broken glass […]

glosses: An individual bet in a parlay (a series of bets where the stake and winnings are cumulatively carried forward).

examples.text: If one leg from your 2-way parlay pushes and the other wins, your parlay bet wins and is paid off as if it's a straight bet (paying -110 or whatever the odds were).

glosses: To remove the legs from an animal carcass.

An advanced or leading position; the lookout.

examples.text: Wolsey sat at the stem more than twenty years.

glosses: The above-ground stalk (technically axis) of a vascular plant, and certain anatomically similar, below-ground organs such as rhizomes, bulbs, tubers, and corms.

examples.text: After they are shot up thirty feet in length, they spread a very large top, having no bough nor twig in the trunk or the stem.

glosses: A slender supporting member of an individual part of a plant such as a flower or a leaf; also, by analogy, the shaft of a feather.

examples.text: the stem of an apple or a cherry

Earless ghost swift moths become “invisible” to echolocating bats by forming mating clusters close (less than half a meter) above vegetation and effectively blending into the clutter of echoes that the bat receives from the leaves and stems around them.

glosses: A narrow part on certain man-made objects, such as a wine glass, a tobacco pipe, a spoon.

The main part of an uninflected word to which affixes may be added to form inflections of the word. A stem often has a more fundamental root. Systematic conjugations and declensions derive from their stems.

A premixed portion of a track for use in audio mastering and remixing.

examples.text: Stem mastering processes a mix by breaking it down into several manageable pieces—that is, stereo stems. The stem approach allows the mastering engineer the opportunity to make larger or smaller changes to separate mix elements before the final compression and limiting are applied to the complete mix.

glosses: The vertical or nearly vertical forward extension of the keel, to which the forward ends of the planks or strakes are attached.
The front part of a vessel.
